newsitem.title: USA: Judge in Ferber case blasts US attorney on Merrill.
newsitem.headline: Judge in Ferber case blasts US attorney on Merrill.

text.p: The federal judge who sentenced municipal banker Mark Ferber to 33 months in prison on Thursday blasted U.S. Attorney Brien O'Connor for not taking stronger action against Ferber's alleged partner in the scheme, Merrill, Lynch & Co.
U.S. Judge William Young, angered that Merrill officials also were not standing before him for sentencing, wanted to know why O'Connor's office indicted Ferber but not Merrill.
Last year, Merrill, along with Ferber's former employer Lazard Freres & Co, agreed to pay a total of $24 million to settle federal kickback charges in the Ferber matter.
O'Connor responded that Merrill Lynch is already in a "highly regulated industry." But Young shot back, "Apparently not regulated enough."
O'Connor then warned that indicting Merrill "could mean the demise of the company and the loss of jobs for thousands of people who had nothing to do ... with the conduct here."
But Judge Young said the deal between Merrill and Lazard "was a kickback scheme ... and kickbacks don't fall out of the sky."
"He was at the gate, and they played him for a sucker," Young said.
O'Connor said Merrill pleaded to his office, "Hit us, but don't kill us." He said Merrill took a "very substantial hit" in terms of finances and public relations.
O'Connor also agreed that Merrill made "several significant changes internally," and both outside and internal counsel at the firm "will keep situations like this one from happening again."
Still, a skeptical Young wanted to know why Merrill had not made public its cleanup effort.
"None of this has appeared in their annual report. I know, I read it," Young said.
